assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design and synthesis of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites links atomic structure directly to function and underpins refining, petrochemistry and emission control at industrial scale. This is the archetype of a designed framework whose structure explains selectivity, and structure-directing-agent concepts have opened many new frameworks.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many groups. Corma (catalytic design and industrial zeolite catalysts), Davis (synthesis and structure-directing concepts, new framework types) and Zones (SDA-based discovery, SSZ materials and Chevron catalysts) represent a coherent synthesis-plus-catalysis configuration; Yu and Tsapatsis are also strong but a three-person limit forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and ubiquitous deployment; recognition is clearly mature, arguably overdue for this class of materials.
uncertainties: The theme is broad, so the exact discovery to be cited is hard to define sharply.
Earlier zeolite and porous-solids contributions (Barrer, Breck, Flanigen) are not on the list, which complicates priority.
I am recalling industrial impact from general knowledge and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers rose from a few percent to over 25 percent certified efficiency within a decade, a striking case of a defect-tolerant, solution-processable structural family with tunable composition. The effect on energy materials research is very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite-sensitized cell, Park the first stable solid-state device with high efficiency, and Snaith the thin-film and mixed-halide efficiency leap. Gratzel, Kanatzidis and Seok are also credible, so credit is contestable and the first-cell versus solid-state-cell distinction matters.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by thousands of groups; efficiency is firmly established. Long-term operational stability, lead toxicity and scale-up remain open, so commercial maturity is not yet proven.
uncertainties: Stability and degradation under operation are unresolved, and the structural origin of ion migration and hysteresis is still debated.
Attribution is crowded and sensitive to how priority is defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large, designed family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selective etching of MAX phases, with tunable surface terminations and applications in energy storage, EMI shielding and sensing. It is a new materials class with a clear structural logic.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Barsoum and Gogotsi made the first Ti3C2 MXene at Drexel, with Gogotsi and Barsoum leading the subsequent expansion. The three-person configuration is natural and clean.
assessment.maturity: The field is young (since 2011) but very active and widely reproduced. Real-world applications are still emerging, so timing may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Surface termination structures are heterogeneous and incompletely characterized, which matters to me as a structural chemist.
Application impact is still largely prospective.
Whether the discovery is mature enough for a prize now.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced proximity degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues opens a new therapeutic modality and drug targets previously considered undruggable. The cereblon mechanism for thalidomide-type drugs gave a mechanistic explanation of a historic drug, and clinical candidates are in trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies proposed and demonstrated PROTACs; Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray and others are also important, and the compound credit across PROTACs and glues may require different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well supported by structures and reproduced widely, but clinical validation is still partial, so timing could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet to my knowledge.
Molecular glues and bifunctional degraders may have different attribution lines.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silicas (MCM-41, SBA-15) showed that supramolecular templating gives uniform pores in the 2-30 nm range, extending molecular sieves beyond the zeolite limit and spawning ordered mesoporous carbons, metal oxides and catalyst supports. Structure was established by diffraction and electron microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Kresge and Beck at Mobil discovered the M41S family; Stucky and Zhao extended to large-pore SBA-15; Ryoo and the Japanese FSM-16 groups also contributed, so priority involves parallel discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over three decades, but practical industrial impact is more modest than zeolites, so the case rests more on the concept.
uncertainties: Parallel FSM-16 work in Japan complicates priority.
Commercial impact is limited relative to scientific influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Crystallographic structures of the Mo-nitrogenase and its FeMo cofactor, including the central carbide, and mechanistic work on N2 reduction address a central problem in bioinorganic chemistry, with structure explaining function.
assessment.attribution: Rees (first structures, MoFe protein, FeMo-co), Einsle (high-resolution structure and interstitial carbide), and Seefeldt (mechanistic studies) form a plausible trio, but Dean, Ribbe and others contributed substantially and the mechanism is not fully settled.
assessment.maturity: Structures are firmly established and independently confirmed; the full catalytic mechanism remains unresolved, so recognition would be for structure rather than mechanism.
uncertainties: The E4 intermediate and substrate-binding mode are still debated.
Recognition for structure versus mechanism could create an awkward framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert one base into another without double-strand breaks, an engineered chemical solution that enlarges genome editing capability; clinical translation is underway. The work is a chemistry-driven protein-nucleic acid engineering advance.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the concept; Komor developed the cytosine base editor and Gaudelli the adenine base editor, which required directed evolution of a deaminase. Nishida and Kondo's earlier related work complicates priority, and Liu appears also on a prime-editing entry.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption and first clinical results, but the field is young and the CRISPR prize in 2020 already recognized the platform.
uncertainties: Overlap with CRISPR recognition and with the prime-editing candidate.
Long-term clinical safety is not yet established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies before radiation damage, closely related to the problem I work on of structures from tiny crystals. It has produced structures of membrane proteins and reaction intermediates.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the diffract-before-destroy demonstration, Hajdu the conceptual foundation, and Fromme the nanocrystal membrane protein work; Schlichting is also important to time-resolved work. The credit configuration is workable.
assessment.maturity: Method is well established with several facilities, but the number of transformative scientific results is smaller than for cryo-EM or synchrotron methods, and access is limited.
uncertainties: Limited breadth of impact compared with cryo-EM and microED.
